articles.title: Manchester United teammates widely share Martínez view that Wilcox is failing
articles.summary: Defender challenged, though, by at least one player. Later insists on social media: ‘I believe in teammates’ Lisandro Martínez’s view that Jason Wilcox is failing as Manchester United’s director of football reflects wider dressing-room frustration over recruitment and squad depth, although the…
body: Martínez may face internal ­disciplinary action over extensive criticism of the hierarchy made in two broadcast interviews after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid. The players had Wednesdayyesterday off so any action would not be taken before their return to training on Thursdaytoday.

Martínez directed his anger at Wilcox and what he referred to as “the top” of the club, saying not enough players had been signed and questioning the scale of investment, and that “more ambition” was needed. He said: “We don’t have the best squad at the moment compared with other top teams.”

Martínez’s comments prompted a challenge from at least one teammate before the flight back to ­Manchester and caused a heightening of tension. The Argentinian did not appear to explicitly call out his teammates, saying merely that “as players we have to do more”, and claimed that last season the squad had “created the base to build an amazing team”.
Although the sway of dressing-room opinion is with Martínez, his remarks are also seen as the centre-back considering his future, because he is out of contract next summer.

articles.title: University of Maryland club tennis team suspended over racist imagery sent to other schools
articles.summary: Image of state flag incorporating KKK hoods was sent to other schools participating in regional tennis tournament. The University of Maryland (UMD) has indefinitely suspended its club tennis team after a graphic featuring Ku Klux Klan imagery was circulated to other universities ahead of a regional…
body: The controversy erupted after Toni Rachal, president of Howard University’s club tennis team, spotted the offensive material in a shared Google document sent to participating schools before last weekend’s tournament, WUSA9 reported.

The graphic features an altered Maryland state flag incorporating images of Ku Klux Klan hoods. Rachal discovered the image while examining a Google document that had been emailed to the tournament’s participating tennis clubs.
In a letter addressed to UMD, Rachal described the imagery as “associated with racial hatred and intimidation” and called for “meaningful accountability” following the incident, WUSA9 reported.

The tennis club at Howard, an HBCU in Washington DC, released a statement on social media describing the image as “a recognizable symbol associated with the Ku Klux Klan”. It questioned how the image made its way into official tournament materials.

articles.title: Martinez outburst came out of 'anger and frustration'
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez says he "spoke out of anger and frustration" when launching a scathing attack on the club's hierarchy.
body: The Argentina international criticised United for not strengthening the squad in the summer following qualification for the Champions League in comments made after the 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League group phase on Tuesday.
Martinez said he expected more investment in the United squad and "more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]".
However, while he stopped short of an apology, he said he has "belief in my team-mates, our manager [Michael Carrick] and everyone working to help this club move forward".
"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted," he wrote in a social media post.

articles.title: Champions League: Mourinho’s Real Madrid stage crazy comeback on Roma return
articles.summary: Mourinho’s side score three late goals from 3-1 deficit. Dortmund latest team beaten in Norway by Bodø/Glimt. José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.
body: Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

But Madrid scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espí, Endrick and the former Roma defender Antonio Rüdiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.
“You could say there were two games in one,” Mourinho said. “Roma were better in all aspects early on. When it was 3-1 everyone probably thought the game was over.”

Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge. The Portuguese coach was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years.

articles.title: PSG on 'different level' - are they building greatest European dynasty?
articles.summary: Paris St-Germain are eyeing a third successive Champions League crown after dismantling Manchester City, but where do they rank against Europe's most dominant clubs?
body: Some find success sweet but fleeting, others spend years building to the pinnacle, and then there are those whose lasting glory evolves into a dynasty.
After tearing Manchester City apart in large spells of their 4-2 Champions League victory on Wednesday, Paris St-Germain look well on track to join the latter bracket.

The back-to-back European champions sliced through City with astonishing ease to take a 3-0 lead into half-time, and were still able to score another despite a spirited second-half fightback from the Premier League leaders.

After obliterating Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2025 final before squeezing past Arsenal on penalties in last season's showpiece game, Luis Enrique's side are aiming to win a third consecutive European crown.

articles.title: Texas Rangers have offseason plan. Does Jacob deGrom fit it?
articles.summary: Jacob deGrom was not the pitcher he wanted to be in 2026, nor the pitcher the Texas Rangers needed him to be. He was one more season on his contract but is a candidate to be traded.
body: Jacob deGrom headed into the offseason full of regret and embarrassment, having let down the Texas Rangers yet again in a critical game. They missed out on the postseason by a game, and he could think of 10 of his starts that should have ended differently.

They were part of his worst season in nearly a decade, before his two Cy Young awards with the Mets in 2018 and 2019. He dealt with a variety of ailments, but he wasn’t seeking excuses. He was seeking fixes for 2027.

The Rangers are seeking fixes, too, with the stated goal of getting younger, healthier, more athletic and mentally tougher. President of baseball operations Chris Young laid out those pillars Sept. 28 during the season wrap-up.

Not known at the time, Young said, was if the Rangers would have to get cheaper. No player on the roster will be paid more in 2027 than the $37 million deGrom will pocket. No player will be older than deGrom, who turns 39 next summer.

articles.title: Trail Blazers reportedly turn to Travis Demers as TV play-by-play voice on game-by-game basis
articles.summary: The Portland Trail Blazers have found their television play-by-play voice for the start of the 2026-27 season (for now, anyway). According to The Oregonian/OregonLive, Travis Demers will be on the call on a game-by-game basis alongside color analyst Lamar Hurd and courtside reporter Brooke…
body: Demers shouldn’t start clearing out the radio booth just yet, though. A league source told The Oregonian that Demers could keep the job for the entire season, but the Blazers are reserving the right to keep shopping. Portland could bring in a temporary play-by-play voice for four or five games at a time during the season, according to the report, allowing the Blazers to audition other broadcasters while giving Demers time off, but Demers could still call every game.

The Blazers are going this route after their previous TV play-by-play hire fell apart in under 24 hours earlier this month. On Oct. 1, Joe Freeman of The Oregonian reported that the team was set to name Braiden Bell its new television play-by-play voice. Bell, a 29-year-old Arizona State graduate, had previously called college basketball on ESPN+ before moving on to the Phoenix Suns’ G League affiliate and the WNBA’s Phoenix Mercury. That night, after KGW reporter Devon Haskins surfaced misogynistic and racist posts Bell had written on Twitter in 2012 and 2013, when he was a teenager, the Blazers announced they would not move forward with him.

articles.title: Man City beaten by PSG in thriller as Guardiola returns to Etihad
articles.summary: Manchester City were beaten 4-2 by a majestic Paris Saint-Germain as Pep Guardiola watched on from the stands in an enthralling Champions League encounter.
body: The reigning back-to-back European champions were keen to make their power felt early at the Etihad, in a game that made clear where the greater concentration of quality resides. Luis Enrique's side were breathtaking in the first half, a masterclass in effortless control with and without the ball.

Desire Doue scored from range. Ousmane Dembele rounded off a wonderful team move 99 seconds later. And Vitinha finished a brilliant first 45 minutes with a thumping finish from Warren Zaire-Emery's instinctive flick. "If you don't go toe-to-toe, you struggle," reflected Enzo Maresca.

A pair of Erling Haaland goals made the scoreline respectable after the interval, and City were good value for both breakthroughs, doing to PSG what had been done to them in the first period. They hit the woodwork a further two times in a half that became increasingly more frantic and transitional.

Despite wave after wave of attack and big chances missed, it was Gianluigi Donnarumma who failed to escape the glare of the spotlight, his poor handling gifting Maghnes Akliouche and the visitors a fourth. He atoned by denying Ferran Torres' woeful penalty attempt late on.

articles.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK
articles.summary: Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick and Florian Wirtz shone after recent criticism as Liverpool thrashed LASK 6-3 to earn their second win in the Champions League.
body: Barcola kick-started his Liverpool career, having not scored or assisted in six appearances since his £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain, while Wirtz responded to calls for him to be dropped with a fine performance in what was expected to be a comfortable evening against the Austrian Bundesliga champions.

Liverpool had 19 shots in the opening period, a new record for an away team in the first half of a Champions League game, as Ronald Araujo headed in his first goal for the club before Barcola got off the mark with a tidy finish and then slotted in another from a Wirtz pass.

Andoni Iraola's side were relentless with Trey Nyoni, 19, impressing in midfield alongside Ryan Gravenberch and they helped add a fourth when Jeremie Frimpong met Kostas Tsimikas' cross with an excellent header that went in off the post just six minutes after the break.

Iraola benched Virgil van Dijk in Austria for only the third time in Liverpool's 39 Champions League games since 2022, but when he and Joe Gomez were introduced at centre-back in the 62nd minute, they conceded three times.
points: Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick and Florian Wirtz shone after recent criticism as Liverpool thrashed LASK 6-3 to earn their second win in the Champions League.
